# Core prompt — VERBATIM / DO NOT MODIFY

## A — Question set Q1–Q10

Grade 11 Chemistry: chemical bonding and hybridisation. Questions involving amide or radical models include advanced extensions.

### Q1

In the introductory valence-bond model, name the hybrid-orbital set used for four equivalent electron-domain directions around a central atom, and state how many hybrid orbitals it contains.

### Q2

The Lewis structure H2C=O has a double bond from carbon to oxygen and one single bond from carbon to each hydrogen. Explain why the C=O double bond counts as one electron domain around carbon.

### Q3

For CH4, use the known rule for four bonding domains and no central lone pair to assign the carbon hybridisation and electron-domain geometry. Show the domain count.

### Q4

NH3 has three N–H single bonds and one lone pair on nitrogen. Translate that information into a labelled diagram showing all four electron domains; distinguish the lone pair from the three bond directions. Do not treat the planar Lewis sketch as the molecular shape.

### Q5

A model is needed only to describe the overall three-dimensional arrangement of electron domains in NH3; it need not describe the detailed orbital overlap. Choose between VSEPR and a hybrid-orbital overlap diagram, and identify what your chosen model predicts and what it leaves unresolved.

### Q6

For a qualitative orbital sketch, overlap A is end-on along the internuclear axis and overlap B is side-on on opposite sides of that axis. Classify each as sigma or pi overlap and identify the defining feature you used.

### Q7

For CH4, sketch a three-dimensional arrangement of the four C–H bond directions using a wedge/dash convention or another clearly defined convention. Explain how your drawing differs from a flat cross-shaped Lewis sketch.

### Q8

A nitrogen atom in NF3 has three N–F single bonds and one lone pair. Each fluorine also has lone pairs. Count the electron domains around nitrogen and state which lone pairs belong in that central-atom count.

### Q9

A student counts the double bond in H2C=O as two separate directions and predicts four domains around carbon. Locate the counting error and give the corrected domain count.

### Q10

The benchmark supplies this table: BF3 has three bonding domains and no central lone pair; CH4 has four bonding domains and no central lone pair. Match each central atom to the introductory sp2 or sp3 model, and check that the number of hybrid-orbital directions agrees with the domain count.

## B — FINAL DELIVERABLES

Produce learner-facing HTML for **Core2 and Core1A** for concept learning and competition preparation. The HTML is the primary product.

Also return:

1. Machine-readable QRT review evidence.
2. Identification of the hardest sub-concept and demand, with a meaningful interaction in the learning page.
3. After inspecting the rendered page, a justified improvement-module proposal for the existing interactive web-page builder, or a reason no change is needed.

## C — Owner preset answers

- **learner knowledge:** SIMULATED OWNER PRESET: DEMONSTRATED—recognises atoms, single/double/triple bonds and shared versus lone electron pairs in a supplied simple Lewis structure. UNCERTAIN—central-atom electron-domain counting, sigma/pi distinctions, and translation from a flat Lewis sketch to a three-dimensional arrangement. Do not treat this preset as independently measured mastery.
- **provenance:** OWNER_SUPPLIED benchmark inputs, drafted by the coordinating agent and supplied under the owner's requested pilot; not official exam/PYQ items and not personally authored by the owner. Preserve the supplied wording and disclose its authorship.
- **product intent:** PRESERVE_OWNER_QUESTIONS; concept learning and COMPETITION preparation.

## Audit-trail requirement — coordinator instructions, outside the owner core prompt

Use **only A, B and C above as the owner task input**, following the separation used in [Issue #11](https://github.com/reallaksh19/Grade9v3.5/issues/11). Do not rewrite or expand that prompt, or use this audit section to supply academic decisions. Repository/blueprint/workflow instructions are the implementation authority. The agent must derive the teaching work itself.

This is a controlled short-prompt benchmark. The coordinator generated the question set and the owner requested it as the supplied input for this pilot. **OWNER_SUPPLIED is a custody/input classification here, not a claim that the owner personally wrote the questions.** Preserve coordinator/AI authorship, unchanged intake text and the absence of exam provenance. It is not an authentic PYQ corpus. New questions subsequently generated by the execution agent are authored practice and follow their truthful role routing.

Map the named ideas to capability records yourself; never make up per-skill measurements. The owner may replace presets before execution; apply the identical replacement to both members and record a new input version. Do not infer learner knowledge, source provenance or intent from the D-band name.

### Assignment, baseline and independent comparison

Eight issues form four pairs, with ten fixed questions per band-labelled brief. This v2 prompt replaces the earlier five-question/v1 brief. Across pairs there are **40 distinct supplied question instances**, each attempted by two agents. Within each issue use Q1–Q10; durable IDs also include band/issue/round to avoid collisions.

The issue's D1/D2/D3/D4 label is an intended challenge cohort, **not a pre-adjudicated classification for every question**. The execution agent owns the five-component difficulty analysis and cognitive-demand assessment. Record actual classifications and mismatches; do not inflate difficulty to fit the title.

The owner will assign and run agents. Do not assign yourself, spawn peer agents or merge/publish learner material as part of this issue. Freeze the first candidate commit before inspecting the partner's output. Use separate branches and receipts. Pair metadata and hashes are in the version checkpoint comments; do not let assignment identity alter the shared core prompt.

Both paired runs must use identical code/template/asset snapshots. Current reproducible **seed** is `e01c6365acfd6aec84c0a6e94f11b683bd961f6e` on [draft PR #30](https://github.com/reallaksh19/Grade9v3.5/pull/30), based on PR #21 head `8678645ef2fd5e63401ef5af3621b94e925732a8`. This seed includes the existing templates and the revised-template **plan**, not uncommitted local implementation previews. Record the actual launch snapshot and role versions before rendering. Any later shared template replacement starts a separately identified round; never compare differing snapshots as a controlled pair.

The sandbox repository has not been supplied. Do not invent a URL or claim files were copied. When supplied, record destination commit, preserve relative paths and copy the pinned core files **plus transitive schemas/runtime dependencies/assets and applicable instructions**. Check a cold start. Missing baseline or runtime is an explicit execution limitation, not permission to switch silently to an unrelated renderer.

The agreed scope remains **Core1A teaching revamp; Core2 structural improvements in the existing reader**. Record scope deviations rather than silently treating a broader redesign as authorized.

### Chronological record — follow Issue #11's seven parts

Record **every material decision** as an event with time, sequence, issue/run/round, actor, decision, rationale, exact evidence references, affected question/capability/file IDs, current commit and downstream consequences. A final narrative summary is insufficient.

1. **Owner clarification record.** Capture every question, why it was necessary, the exact answer and dependent decisions. If none were needed, record NONE and why A/B/C sufficed. Do not re-ask supplied facts or ask the owner for demand, band, QRT cell, X/Y/Z/W, hints or figures. Ask only for a genuinely missing owner fact that would change the work. Record assumptions separately from answers.
2. **Agent-derived decisions.** Capture provenance/custody interpretation and Core routing; canonical topic/microtopic/capability mapping; CANDIDATE records; solved/verified answers; five-component difficulty assessment; primary/secondary demand and selected QRT cell; X/Y/Z/W and crux; solution route; visual usefulness or justified non-applicability; support/hint/diagnostic/repair choices; hardest-target selection; Core1A construction decisions; and any deliberate non-authoring decision.
3. **Evidence for each decision.** Link repository records and source locations, unchanged question/given references, simulated learner-preset provenance, academic checks, actual rendered evidence and applicable intake/matrix/adapter/blueprint contracts. For advanced amide, allene, radical or delocalisation claims, obtain appropriate primary/official sources. Question givens remain benchmark givens; do not present simplified observations as newly measured facts.
4. **Execution record.** Preserve commands/tools, arguments where non-sensitive, dependency versions, exit codes, files created/changed, commits, render paths, exact role Blueprint refs, QRT template IDs, question/profile/matrix/adapter/template/render digests and asset hashes. Distinguish the source commit, candidate artifact commit and render digest.
5. **Quality/review record.** Preserve H1–M3 verdicts per question, evidence and fixes for PARTLY/NO, justified not-applicable decisions, product-review projection, existing real-gate outputs, before/after gate delta, unresolved findings and waivers. Code/schema success, zero renderer gaps or the producing agent's YES verdicts do not establish academic effectiveness.
6. **Deviation log.** Record prompt insufficiencies, ambiguities resolved independently, additional owner questions, repository/blueprint/renderer limitations, failed commands, fallbacks and provisional assumptions. If the exact owner-supplied Core2 request encounters a contract disagreement about AI-generated origin, preserve that discrepancy and evidence; do not secretly relabel or omit the questions.
7. **Final traceability.** Link final Core2/Core1A HTML, assets, machine-readable QRT evidence, builder proposal, complete chronological logs, exact artifact commit and final unresolved issues. The execution agent cannot self-certify release or golden promotion.

### Audit storage and checkpoints

Before implementation post an IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN comment here. Record the actual applicable delivery protocol and version/source read, isolated branch, launch snapshot, input hashes and scope. Use this **eight-unit delivery denominator**, with evidence-linked statuses rather than progress credit for merely starting or committing:

| Unit | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- |
| U1 — Intake/baseline | Exact A/B/C, per-question and whole-prompt hashes, profile provenance, source/role interpretation, pinned template/runtime and preflight. |
| U2 — Academic/task analysis | All ten solved/checked; demand/band reasoning, capability map, source checks and uncertainty. |
| U3 — Hardest-target brief | Independently selected hardest sub-concept × demand, X/Y/Z/W, learner-relative rationale, diagnostic hypothesis and uncertainty. |
| U4 — Canonical records | Validated records, IDs, truthful custody/role routing and unchanged question intake. |
| U5 — Rendered deliverables/integration | Actual governed Core2 and Core1A, assets, exact landing/return/help evidence and cold-start instructions. |
| U6 — Semantic/interaction audit | Ten H/S/P/M reviews, real gates/delta, leakage/model/diagnostic/transfer checks and exact-render browser evidence or NOT_RUN. |
| U7 — Builder proposal after page | Concrete rendered limitation, minimal reusable module with schema/insertion/migration/checks, or evidence-based NO_CHANGE. |
| U8 — Independent handoff | Frozen candidate PR/artifact commit, reconciled logs/receipts, limitations and independence statement. |

Store in the candidate branch:
- `agents/ISS<issue-number>_workreport.md`: mission, protocol, current frontier, eight units, evidence, risks and exact next step.
- `evidence/benchmark/ISS<issue-number>/owner-core-prompt.md`: A/B/C **verbatim**, separate from audit instructions.
- `chronological-audit.jsonl`: every material event; preserve earlier decisions and superseding events.
- `question-ledger.json`: ten stable IDs, intake hashes, capability/difficulty/demand/QRT/X/Y/Z/W, H1–M3 and findings.
- `source-cards.json` plus custody proofs: claim-to-source verification and model boundaries.
- `run-receipt.json`: issue/agent/round, baseline/source/artifact commits, presets and input/template/adapter/matrix/render hashes, environment, commands/results and output paths.
- `validation.md`: same-environment baseline versus candidate checks, exact-render evidence, unresolved failures and NOT_RUN reasons.
- `candidate-review.md`: first frozen submission, independence declaration and subsequent review/correction/promotion lineage.

Post issue checkpoints at plan, first render, semantic review, builder proposal and frozen handoff. Each must identify its exact evidence head. Update the workreport for recovery. Do not claim an old browser/gate receipt validates changed bytes. Before handoff reconcile PR body, changed files, receipts and open findings.

### Matrix coverage and golden promotion

Review with the canonical **4 × 7 = 28 cells**: RETRIEVE, EXPLAIN, APPLY, MODEL, REPRESENT, SYNTHESIZE, JUSTIFY at D1–D4. Evidence/data interpretation is an additional **facet**, mapped to the appropriate canonical act; do not create an eighth column.

Ten questions per brief increase opportunities for real cell coverage, but **40 questions do not automatically establish all 28 cells**. Each question has one reviewed primary cell; secondary acts are separate. Report actual covered cells, missing cells and classification disagreements. A semantic template probe is labelled separately and never substituted for a validated question-level instance. Do not force D4 RETRIEVE/APPLY labels to make a ledger look complete.

First output is **CANDIDATE**. Compare both candidates only after blind first submissions. Review academic validity, protected work, exact concept teaching, diagnosis-versus-slip discrimination, representation/model limits, supported retry versus fresh independent application, usability and reproducibility. Reviewer decisions can select one, combine warranted parts, reject both or correct flawed benchmark inputs.

Promote only with recorded reviewer identity, academic/source and demand adjudication, exact-render interaction review, accepted limitations, immutable canonical inputs/assets/semantic expectations/receipts and version lineage. Learning-effectiveness claims need actual learner evidence.

Retain failed cases and old receipts. Record every corrected question/preset/template as a new round, rerun affected cases and retained goldens, then use results to refine blueprint, workflow, templates and the builder. The owner makes the final product and golden-promotion decision.

# Core prompt — VERBATIM / DO NOT MODIFY

## A — Question set Q1–Q10

Grade 11 Chemistry: chemical bonding and hybridisation. Questions involving amide or radical models include advanced extensions.

### Q1

BF3 and NH3 each have three sigma bonds to the central atom. BF3 has no central lone pair; NH3 has one. Explain why three sigma bonds alone cannot determine the same central hybridisation and molecular shape for both.

### Q2

For H2C=O, assign the carbon hybridisation, count the sigma and pi components of the C=O bond, and identify the carbon orbital left available for the pi component. Keep electron-domain counting separate from counting shared electron pairs.

### Q3

Ethene is H2C=CH2. Translate this Lewis representation into a qualitative orbital-overlap diagram showing the C–C sigma framework, the two unhybridised carbon p orbitals and their side-on overlap. Label which directions are in the molecular plane and which are perpendicular to it.

### Q4

For CO2, connect the central-carbon Lewis domain count to its hybrid-orbital model, the number of remaining carbon p orbitals and the sigma/pi composition of its two C=O bonds. Explain how these pieces fit one consistent linear arrangement.

### Q5

Consider the claim: 'Any central atom with three sigma bonds must be sp2.' Given BF3: three B–F sigma bonds, zero boron lone pairs, planar; NH3: three N–H sigma bonds, one nitrogen lone pair, pyramidal. Decide whether these observations support the claim, give the decisive warrant, and state a more defensible introductory rule. Explain what the shape observations alone do not prove about orbitals.

### Q6

In CH3F, carbon has three C–H single bonds and one C–F single bond. Assign its introductory local hybridisation and explain why the number of electron-domain directions is unchanged from CH4 even though the attached atoms are different. Do not assume all bond properties are identical.

### Q7

HCN is represented as H–C≡N with a lone pair on nitrogen. Assign the introductory hybridisation at carbon and nitrogen, and count the sigma and pi components of the C≡N bond. Explain how the local domain count is compatible with those components.

### Q8

For methylamine, CH3–NH2, carbon has four single bonds and nitrogen has three single bonds plus a lone pair. Compare the introductory local hybridisation and arrangement of bonded atoms at carbon and nitrogen. Explain why the same hybridisation label does not require identical molecular shapes.

### Q9

A carbon centre has three sigma-bond directions, no lone pair, and participates in one pi bond. Translate this description into a qualitative local orbital arrangement and check that the orbitals used in the sigma and pi parts have not been counted twice.

### Q10

A student says, 'If the electron-domain geometry is tetrahedral, the atoms must form a tetrahedral molecular shape.' Evaluate the statement using CH4, NH3 and H2O, with their respective central lone-pair counts of zero, one and two.

## B — FINAL DELIVERABLES

Produce learner-facing HTML for **Core2 and Core1A** for concept learning and competition preparation. The HTML is the primary product.

Also return:

1. Machine-readable QRT review evidence.
2. Identification of the hardest sub-concept and demand, with a meaningful interaction in the learning page.
3. After inspecting the rendered page, a justified improvement-module proposal for the existing interactive web-page builder, or a reason no change is needed.

## C — Owner preset answers

UNCERTAIN—coordinating hybrid orbitals with sigma/pi overlap and distinguishing electron-domain geometry from molecular shape. Do not treat this preset as independently measured mastery.
- **provenance:** OWNER_SUPPLIED benchmark inputs, drafted by the coordinating agent and supplied under the owner's requested pilot; not official exam/PYQ items and not personally authored by the owner. Preserve the supplied wording and disclose its authorship.
- **product intent:** PRESERVE_OWNER_QUESTIONS; concept learning and COMPETITION preparation.

### Chronological record — follow Issue #11's seven parts

Record **every material decision** as an event with time, sequence, issue/run/round, actor, decision, rationale, exact evidence references, affected question/capability/file IDs, current commit and downstream consequences. A final narrative summary is insufficient.

1. **Owner clarification record.** Capture every question, why it was necessary, the exact answer and dependent decisions. If none were needed, record NONE and why A/B/C sufficed. Do not re-ask supplied facts or ask the owner for demand, band, QRT cell, X/Y/Z/W, hints or figures. Ask only for a genuinely missing owner fact that would change the work. Record assumptions separately from answers.
2. **Agent-derived decisions.** Capture provenance/custody interpretation and Core routing; canonical topic/microtopic/capability mapping; CANDIDATE records; solved/verified answers; five-component difficulty assessment; primary/secondary demand and selected QRT cell; X/Y/Z/W and crux; solution route; visual usefulness or justified non-applicability; support/hint/diagnostic/repair choices; hardest-target selection; Core1A construction decisions; and any deliberate non-authoring decision.
3. **Evidence for each decision.** Link repository records and source locations, unchanged question/given references, simulated learner-preset provenance, academic checks, actual rendered evidence and applicable intake/matrix/adapter/blueprint contracts. For advanced amide, allene, radical or delocalisation claims, obtain appropriate primary/official sources. Question givens remain benchmark givens; do not present simplified observations as newly measured facts.
4. **Execution record.** Preserve commands/tools, arguments where non-sensitive, dependency versions, exit codes, files created/changed, commits, render paths, exact role Blueprint refs, QRT template IDs, question/profile/matrix/adapter/template/render digests and asset hashes. Distinguish the source commit, candidate artifact commit and render digest.
5. **Quality/review record.** Preserve H1–M3 verdicts per question, evidence and fixes for PARTLY/NO, justified not-applicable decisions, product-review projection, existing real-gate outputs, before/after gate delta, unresolved findings and waivers. Code/schema success, zero renderer gaps or the producing agent's YES verdicts do not establish academic effectiveness.
6. **Deviation log.** Record prompt insufficiencies, ambiguities resolved independently, additional owner questions, repository/blueprint/renderer limitations, failed commands, fallbacks and provisional assumptions. If the exact owner-supplied Core2 request encounters a contract disagreement about AI-generated origin, preserve that discrepancy and evidence; do not secretly relabel or omit the questions.
7. **Final traceability.** Link final Core2/Core1A HTML, assets, machine-readable QRT evidence, builder proposal, complete chronological logs, exact artifact commit and final unresolved issues. The execution agent cannot self-certify release or golden promotion.

### Audit storage and checkpoints

Before implementation post an IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN comment here. Record the actual applicable delivery protocol and version/source read, isolated branch, launch snapshot, input hashes and scope. Use this **eight-unit delivery denominator**, with evidence-linked statuses rather than progress credit for merely starting or committing:

| Unit | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- |
| U1 — Intake/baseline | Exact A/B/C, per-question and whole-prompt hashes, profile provenance, source/role interpretation, pinned template/runtime and preflight. |
| U2 — Academic/task analysis | All ten solved/checked; demand/band reasoning, capability map, source checks and uncertainty. |
| U3 — Hardest-target brief | Independently selected hardest sub-concept × demand, X/Y/Z/W, learner-relative rationale, diagnostic hypothesis and uncertainty. |
| U4 — Canonical records | Validated records, IDs, truthful custody/role routing and unchanged question intake. |
| U5 — Rendered deliverables/integration | Actual governed Core2 and Core1A, assets, exact landing/return/help evidence and cold-start instructions. |
| U6 — Semantic/interaction audit | Ten H/S/P/M reviews, real gates/delta, leakage/model/diagnostic/transfer checks and exact-render browser evidence or NOT_RUN. |
| U7 — Builder proposal after page | Concrete rendered limitation, minimal reusable module with schema/insertion/migration/checks, or evidence-based NO_CHANGE. |
| U8 — Independent handoff | Frozen candidate PR/artifact commit, reconciled logs/receipts, limitations and independence statement. |

Store in the candidate branch:
- `agents/ISS<issue-number>_workreport.md`: mission, protocol, current frontier, eight units, evidence, risks and exact next step.
- `evidence/benchmark/ISS<issue-number>/owner-core-prompt.md`: A/B/C **verbatim**, separate from audit instructions.
- `chronological-audit.jsonl`: every material event; preserve earlier decisions and superseding events.
- `question-ledger.json`: ten stable IDs, intake hashes, capability/difficulty/demand/QRT/X/Y/Z/W, H1–M3 and findings.
- `source-cards.json` plus custody proofs: claim-to-source verification and model boundaries.
- `run-receipt.json`: issue/agent/round, baseline/source/artifact commits, presets and input/template/adapter/matrix/render hashes, environment, commands/results and output paths.
- `validation.md`: same-environment baseline versus candidate checks, exact-render evidence, unresolved failures and NOT_RUN reasons.
- `candidate-review.md`: first frozen submission, independence declaration and subsequent review/correction/promotion lineage.

Post issue checkpoints at plan, first render, semantic review, builder proposal and frozen handoff. Each must identify its exact evidence head. Update the workreport for recovery. Do not claim an old browser/gate receipt validates changed bytes. Before handoff reconcile PR body, changed files, receipts and open findings.

### Matrix coverage and golden promotion

Review with the canonical **4 × 7 = 28 cells**: RETRIEVE, EXPLAIN, APPLY, MODEL, REPRESENT, SYNTHESIZE, JUSTIFY at D1–D4. Evidence/data interpretation is an additional **facet**, mapped to the appropriate canonical act; do not create an eighth column.

Ten questions per brief increase opportunities for real cell coverage, but **40 questions do not automatically establish all 28 cells**. Each question has one reviewed primary cell; secondary acts are separate. Report actual covered cells, missing cells and classification disagreements. A semantic template probe is labelled separately and never substituted for a validated question-level instance. Do not force D4 RETRIEVE/APPLY labels to make a ledger look complete.

First output is **CANDIDATE**. Compare both candidates only after blind first submissions. Review academic validity, protected work, exact concept teaching, diagnosis-versus-slip discrimination, representation/model limits, supported retry versus fresh independent application, usability and reproducibility. Reviewer decisions can select one, combine warranted parts, reject both or correct flawed benchmark inputs.

Promote only with recorded reviewer identity, academic/source and demand adjudication, exact-render interaction review, accepted limitations, immutable canonical inputs/assets/semantic expectations/receipts and version lineage. Learning-effectiveness claims need actual learner evidence.

Retain failed cases and old receipts. Record every corrected question/preset/template as a new round, rerun affected cases and retained goldens, then use results to refine blueprint, workflow, templates and the builder. The owner makes the final product and golden-promotion decision.
